data.narrative:
Reaction Dynamics is a Series A stage space and aerospace company founded by Bachar Elzein. The valuation framework draws on a comparables universe of 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-stage companies including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, though narrow peer-set constraints limit the applicability of multiple methods.

Only one valuation method is defensible given available data. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the company's $38M total raised, treated as a proxy for Series A valuation, yielding $76M. Peer-median anchoring is inapplicable: while 14 same-sector peers exist, none of the refined subsets (same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar-tier) contain the three minimum datapoints required for statistical reliability. Public-comp P/S anchoring cannot be executed because target revenue is not disclosed—a standard constraint for private company analysis.

The triangulation supports a median valuation of $76M, with a reasonable range of $65M (low) to $87M (high) derived from sensitivity around the stage-progression multiplier. The analysis carries two material uncertainties: the absence of tight peer multiples in the frontier aerospace segment limits cross-check confidence, and undisclosed revenue prevents revenue-based valuation benchmarking against public comparables trading at a 26.4x sector P/S median. Further diligence on unit economics and product-market traction would be required to narrow this range.
